newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 10.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Treasury crime report ridiculed: Police Minister Jack Elder on Wednesday laughed off a Treasury report that says employing more police officers will add to justice system costs because more officers would catch more criminals. Page 1.

Delamere drug call gets mixed reaction: Associate Treasurer Tuariki Delamere's call to decriminalise cannabis has won him praise from the pro-cannabis lobby -- and sparked fierce debate among his colleagues. Page 1.

NZ First sees Budget, order as restoring confidence: NZ First MPs are pinning their hopes on the Budget and a renewed focus on self-discipline to restore confidence in their party, which has sunk in public opinion since it entered the Coalition Government. Page 2.

Official's work trip cost under $4800: The Consumer Affairs Ministry officials who accompanied Consumer Affairs Minister Robyn McDonald to an Internet business conference in Paris spent just under $4800 on his trip and managed to attend two other conferences as well. Page 2.
Super summit proposed: ACT NZ deputy leader Ken Shirley wants the political heat taken out of the compulsory superannuation debate with a one-day multi-party summit to thrash out the issues. Page 2.
Labour MPs given Maori advice: Labour MPs have been told a constitutional convention is needed to fully debate the Treaty of Waitangi and how it applies to all New Zealanders. Page 2.

Mergers ruled out for Aussie banks: The Australian Government's decision to rule out mergers between Australia's four largest banks -- all with operations in New Zealand -- should not stop further downsizing here, Commerce Minister John Luxton said on Wednesday. Page 13.

Kiwi rates most over-valued -- bank: Investment bank Goldman Sachs says the New Zealand dollar's cross rates against the mark and the yen are the two most over-valued exchange rates in the developed world. Page 13.

Dollar's value and deficit fail to shake Birch's pitch: The dollar was not over-valued, New Zealand warranted an improved credit rating, and he was not worried by the current account deficit, Finance Minister Bill Birch said in Hong Kong on Wednesday. Page 13.

Warehouse profit improves: The Warehouse Group has posted a profit of $25.2 million for the half-year to January 1997, 55 percent higher than last year's and above market expectations. Brokers were forecasting a result of between $17 million and $20 million for the six months. Page 13.

Tranzrich in bus franchise move: Masterton-based Tranzrich Travel has applied to the Commerce Commission to buy the Intercity bus franchise and related assets of Guthrey's Intercity Coach Services. Page 13.
Inflation forecast called "phoney": Wellngton-based forecasting group Berl says the Reserve Bank's medium-term forecasts of lower inflation are "simply phoney". Page 13.

Fixed mortgages to rise: ANZ Bank and PostBank are joining the move to raise fixed mortgage rates. That brings to six the number of large banks which have increased their mortgage interest rates over the past few days. Page 13.
Caroma seeks clearance: Caroma Industries has applied to the Commerce Commission for clearance to acquire James Hardie Building Products' bathroom products operations. Page 13.
NEW ZEALAND HERALD
State landlord lashed by ministry: Eviction threats 'used to collect bank rent': The Ministry of Housing has criticised the state landlord, Housing New Zealand, for heavy-handed tactics with tenants.

Decision greeted with relief: The Australian Government's decision to keep the walls largely intact around its financial sector was greeted with relief and astonishment by differing interests in New Zealand's financial community on Wednesday.
Time for SI ports to work together, says Lyttelton: Lyttelton Port Company is keen to lead what it sees as the unevitable rationalisation of the South Island port industry.

Waltus to raise nearly $22m for Albany joint venture project: Lower Hutt-based property syndicator Waltus Investments will take on its first development joint venture with the launch next week of a prospectus to raise $21.8 million for the Albany power centre shopping development north of Auckland.

Metropolitan sights home care: The Metropolitan Lifecare Group has purchased one of the country's largest contracts to provide home-care health services to aging people as a result of buying the Powley House retirement village in Blockhouse Bay.
Lion closes Australian brewery: Lion Nathan Australia said on Wednesday it was closing its Grafton Brewery in New South Wales, affecting 42 staff.
Cultus discovery to be appraised: Shareholders in Cultus Petroleum have been reminded the company is a long way from realising the potential of recent oil and gas discoveries.
THE PRESS

Police seek tough drug directive: The police need a firm policy directive from the government on whether they should get serious about policing cannabis use, Police Association president Greg O'Connor says. Page 1.
Pure NZ head eyes technology activities: Pure New Zealand will be moving further towards intellectual property and other technology activities under its new chief executive, Chris Holmes. Page 27

Richina says returns from China still some way off: Richina Pacific shareholders will have to wait some time before the company's investments in China deliver the profits hoped for, says chairman Jim Syme. Page 27.

DFI decision due Monday: A decision on Goodman Fielder's application for approval to buy the milling and baking assets Christchurch-based Defiance Food Industries will be made before 5pm on Monday (NZ time), says the Commerce Commission. Page 27.

CHH Copec efforts 'frustrated': Carter Holt Harvey's chief executive, John Faraci, said on Wednesday his company has been left "frustrated" by its continuing inability to secure any management control of its joint venture with Cia De Petroleos de Chile SA (Copec). Page 28.
